title: Presentation design: contrast, alignment, repetition and whitespace

videos.script: You do not need to be a designer to make a slide look clear. You need four principles, and they fit on one hand. {{four}} Contrast. If two things are different, make them very different, so the eye knows what to read first. {{contrast}} Alignment. Every element lines up with something else. Nothing sits where it happened to land. {{alignment}} Repetition. The same thing looks the same on every slide. The same colour means the same thing. {{repetition}} And whitespace. Things that belong together sit together, and the empty space between groups does the organising. {{space}} None of this is decoration. Each principle removes a small decision the audience would otherwise make while you are talking. {{work}} This lesson applies all four to Faro's deck, and ends with the question of how much text a slide should carry at all. {{text}}
